newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Queensland says no electricity privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Queensland says no electricity privatisation.

text.p: Queensland has no plan privatise electricity assets as part of its reform of the power industry, Mines and Energy minister Tom Gilmore said on Wednesday.

"The Queensland government's commitment to public ownership of state-owned assets, if anything, is the clearest demonstration of its confidence in the (electricity) market," Gilmore told an electricity conference.
"Our commitment to the market is far more comprehensive than a simple restructuring exercise," he said. "(There will be) no privatisation - I repeat, no privatisation," he said.
Gilmore said the state government's decision to retain electricity assets in public ownership was a significant indication of its confidence in the electricity market.
"The privatisation debate has served only to distract attention from what is a robust plan for Queensland's electricity industry, and not just for government-owned assets," he said.

The government's electricity plan would instead be based on independent regulation of natural monopoly industry elements and surrendering responsibility for balancing supply-demand dynamics to market forces, he said.
